title: Trump Threatens Kennedy Center Closure in Heated Feud Over Naming Rights
snippet: President Donald Trump warned the iconic Kennedy Center could be 'ripped down' if his administration is not granted official recognition on the performing arts venue.
content:
WASHINGTON — In an escalating dispute over Washington's premier cultural venue, Donald Trump warned on Wednesday that the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts could be shuttered or even "ripped down" if his administration does not receive official recognition for its oversight and funding efforts.

Speaking with reporters on an airport tarmac in North Carolina, Trump claimed the landmark institution had been plagued by financial mismanagement prior to his involvement. "I think that the Trump administration should certainly have recognition," Trump insisted, asserting that without it, the venue's long-term survival is at risk.

Court Order and Emergency Shutdown

Trump's comments come on the heels of a federal court decision blocking the performing arts center's board from adding a tribute to him on the premises. Following the ruling, Trump countered by threatening to freeze $257 million in congressionally authorized renovation funding unless the building incorporates his name.

Shortly after the judge issued the injunction, the center's board—composed largely of Trump appointees—voted to immediately close the facility to undergo emergency repairs, pointing to a recent incident where plaster fell from a foyer ceiling during heavy rain. By Wednesday morning, temporary construction fencing was already being installed around the main entrance.

Lawmakers and Kennedy Relatives Push Back

The sudden closure sparked swift outrage on Capitol Hill and from descendants of President John F. Kennedy. Rep. Joyce Beatty, D-Ohio, characterized Trump's reaction as an attempt to bypass judicial authority.

"He threw a tantrum because he lost in court," Beatty told reporters following a tense meeting on the House steps, accusing the administration of acting in contempt of the judicial ruling. Meanwhile, members of the Kennedy family publicly criticized the standoff, accusing Trump of holding the national cultural treasure hostage over personal pride.
